question: What is the minimum passing mark in the end semester examination and overall course?
expected_answer: A candidate must secure a minimum of 45% marks in the end-semester examination and a minimum of 50% marks in continuous internal assessment and end-semester examination put together.

[4. EXAMINATION ADMINISTRATION AND PROCEDURES]
Source: https://cit.edu.in/coe/about-the-office-of-the-controller-of-examinations The Office of the Controller of Examinations (COE) "plays a vital role in safeguarding the academic credibility of the Institute. It is responsible for planning, administering, and monitoring all examination-related activities, ensuring that assessment processes are conducted with fairness, accuracy, and transparency." Key responsibilities listed on the page: - Conduct of Examinations: planning and administering all internal and end-semester examinations in accordance with the approved academic schedule for every programme. - Appointment of Examiners: identifying and appointing competent faculty members and external experts for question paper preparation and theory paper evaluation. - Assessment of Practical and Project Work: constituting specialized Examination Committees to evaluate laboratory examinations, project reviews, and viva-voce assessments. - Result Compilation and Declaration: processing, verification and finalization of results, followed by official publication after approval by the Result Passing Board (RPB). - Issue of Academic Records: official grade sheets and academic statements. - Academic Reporting: performance analysis reports presented to the Academic Council. - Recommendation for Degree Award: verifying eligibility and recommending qualified candidates for degrees. Additional services: certified transcripts and duplicate academic records; verification of certificates and mark statements; organizing the Annual Graduation Day. Office administration: headed by the Controller of Examinations, assisted by a Deputy Controller, supported by thirteen staff members. Named officials (source: https://cit.edu.in/about-us/autonomous-status): Dr. R. Sriram, Controller of Examinations; Dr. R. Sathyanarayan Sridhar, Deputy Controller of Examinations. expected_answer: The maximum period permitted is 7 years (14 semesters) for students admitted in the first year, and 6 years (12 semesters) for lateral entry students.
